sources.entry: Escale - Native SSH client with tabs, an SFTP browser beside the terminal, tunnels, multi-execution and a built-in X11 server. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ATTILA-KRB/escale) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Escale is a free, native macOS SSH client that combines terminal sessions, an SFTP file pane, port tunnels, multi-host command execution and a built-in X11 server in one window.
summary.what_it_does: Escale is a session manager for macOS that drives the system's OpenSSH (/usr/bin/ssh) through one ControlMaster connection per host, so existing ~/.ssh/config, ProxyJump, agents and FIDO keys work unchanged. It provides tabs, split panes and detachable tabs with automatic reconnection. A sidebar SFTP pane reuses the existing connection, follows the terminal's current folder, supports drag and drop with Finder, a transfer queue, server-to-server copy and remote file editing. Local, remote and dynamic (SOCKS) tunnels can be opened and edited while running, and the port is probed before showing as active. It can broadcast keystrokes to panes, tabs or a selection, or run one command across a group of hosts and report output, exit code and duration per host. Extras include macros bound to ⌃⌥1 to ⌃⌥9, quick connect, host import from MobaXterm, PuTTY, Termius, CSV or ssh config, optional Telnet, serial, VNC and RDP support, and an opt-in MCP interface for AI agents with per-host permission levels.
use_cases: manage several remote servers in one window
transfer files to and from a remote server with drag and drop
open local, remote or SOCKS tunnels to remote hosts
run the same command on a group of servers in parallel
run remote graphical apps on a Mac without installing XQuartz
import saved sessions from MobaXterm, PuTTY or Termius
how_to_run: Download the notarized disk image from the Releases page, open it and drag Escale to Applications (requires macOS 15 or later).
git clone the repository (URL is blank in the README), then cd escale
scripts/test.sh (core tests and a Debug build)
notable: Drives the system OpenSSH, so ~/.ssh/config, ProxyJump and agents work as they are; Escale never writes to ~/.ssh
Tunnels are probed before being shown as active, so a refused forward is not reported as open
Built-in X11 server starts on demand, listens on no network port and needs no XQuartz install
Broadcast typing and parallel multi-host command runs, with host values shell-escaped
Opt-in MCP server for AI agents, off by default, with read-only, confirm, or free per-host levels and logged calls
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later; not available on the Mac App Store because the sandbox blocks system OpenSSH and ~/.ssh/config
Building from source needs Xcode with Swift 6 and downloads a roughly 120 MB XQuartz installer on first build
Signing and notarization require your own Apple Developer ID; the README notes the release doc is written in French
Debug builds are ad-hoc signed with updates disabled
